incident-bot: Pager triggered for service=auth.validate severity=high — reason=jwt-kid-mismatch (pagerduty:PD-789)
pagerduty: Incident PD-789 opened · https://pd.example.com/incidents/PD-789 · paging nina, ops-oncall
nina: acked in PD. i'm looking at graphs and logs now.
ops-oncall: joining. quick read: client error spike on token validation starting ~14:21 UTC in ap-south and eu-central.
rahul: logs from auth-validate show repeated failures: `signature verification error: unknown kid k-7777` across many hosts. JWKS probe shows old payload.
sre-kyla: i hit the jwks url directly in eu-central and get only two keys: k-101 and k-202. new key k-7777 not present. curl:
```
$ curl -s https://auth.redwood.example/.well-known/jwks.json | jq '.keys[].kid'
"k-101"
"k-202"
```
nina: our key-rotation pipeline indicates it completed at 14:18 UTC and uploaded jwks to GCS. but CDN logs show no purge event for the jwks path.
ops-oncall: if CDN cached the old JWKS blob, validators will keep failing until TTL expires. mitigation plan: 1) enable validator fallback to accept last-known-good for 15m; 2) explicitly purge CDN for jwks path; 3) re-publish jwks to origin if purge fails. doing step 1 now.
rahul: toggled `ALLOW_PREV_SIGNING_KEY=true` via feature flag service — propagation to validators in progress.
support: posting external note: "Some authentication attempts may fail; engineers investigating." link: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/PD-789
sre-kyla: running CDN purge via infra-admin: `curl -X POST https://cdn-api.example/purge -d '{"path":"/.well-known/jwks.json"}'`
nina: purge returned 202 Accepted with job id purge-889.
ops-oncall: purging CDN done. waiting for edge invalidation — ETA ~30s.
rahul: in the meantime clearing in-memory jwks cache on validate pods across clusters:
```
for c in ap-south eu-central us-west; do kubectl --context $c -n prod get pods -l app=auth-validate -o name | xargs -I{} kubectl --context $c -n prod exec {} -- curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/cache/jwks/clear; done
```
sre-kyla: small flurry of 500s during cache clear but auth returns recovering immediately.
nina: re-checking jwks origin bucket: file present and contains k-7777. CDN purge logs show success after 00:00:28. edge now returns new key.
```
$ curl -s https://auth.redwood.example/.well-known/jwks.json | jq '.keys[].kid'
"k-101"
"k-202"
"k-7777"
```
ops-oncall: verified with a signed token — validation succeeds. error rate back to baseline.
status-bot: Status updated: "Authentication failures resolved; mitigation applied. Root cause under investigation." link: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/PD-789
nina: quick RCA hypothesis: rotation pipeline uploaded JWKS to origin but CDN purge step failed silently due to missing API token renewal in rotation job. rotation job reported success, but did not validate edge presence. filed immediate action items.
rahul: immediate next actions: 1) make rotation job fail on CDN-purge failure; 2) add post-rotation verification that jwks appears at edge within 60s in at least 2 regions; 3) add alert for jwks endpoint mismatch between origin and edge.
sre-kyla: i'll own the CDN purge hardening and add retries; nina will own rotation job changes; ops-oncall will add monitoring alert.
ops-oncall: updating PD timeline and moving to monitoring for 20m. switching incident state.
pagerduty: PD-789 status changed to Monitoring by ops-oncall
support: CSMs notified for affected tenants; drafted customer message template.
nina: customer-impact window estimated 14:18–14:24 UTC. i'll draft postmortem and schedule follow-up.
ops-oncall: great response — keeping an eye for any re-occurrence. closing thread once postmortem link published. :white_check_mark:
